what: The Unit Price Comparer tells you which product is really the cheapest when packs come in different sizes. Enter the price and size of each option, including multipacks, and it works out the price per kilogram, 100 g, liter, ounce, item or meter and highlights the best value.
You can mix units such as grams and pounds or milliliters and gallons; everything is converted before comparing.
uses: Compare a 500 g bag with a 1 kg bag.
Check whether the big pack really saves money.
Compare cost per roll, per wash or per item.
Compare price per liter or gallon.
tutorial: Pick what to compare per, such as kilogram, 100 g or liter.
Type an optional name, the price, the size and its unit.
Type the size of one pack and the number of packs.
Press "Add another product" for as many as you like.
Each product shows its unit price; the best value is highlighted and the others show how much more they cost.
features: Grams, kilograms, ounces, pounds, milliliters, liters, fluid ounces, gallons, items and lengths.
With the percentage more for each other option.
Shows how much you save buying the best option.
Switches the comparison unit to match your products.

example.title: Worked example: three bags of rice
example.text: A 500 g bag costs 2.49, a 1 kg bag costs 4.29 and a 6 × 250 g multipack costs 5.99. Per kg that is 4.98, 4.29 and 3.99, so the multipack is the best value, and the small bag costs about 25% more.

tips: Shelf labels sometimes use different units for neighbouring products; this tool evens them out.
Only buy bulk if you will use it before it expires.
Compare per 100 g for small items like spices.
Weight and volume cannot be compared directly.
problems: It is sold by a different kind of unit (weight vs volume). Change the unit or the comparison.
Packs must be a whole number
Type the number of packs as 1, 2, 3 and so on.
The products really cost the same per unit.
